_doc: Cross-investor rulings for the Menlo run (COLLECTION.md 10 and 12). `distinct` pairs are two companies the loose name key joined; `accepted` pairs are one company where the two published rows disagree for a reason recorded here. Menlo's fifty-year book collides with every sibling base on common words — Amplitude, Alloy, Axiom, Canvas, Check, Clarify, Glide — because the 1980s and 1990s rows carry names the 2010s and 2020s reused. Written at the investor level; the shared file is written only at wave alignment.

distinct.note: AMPLITUDE SOFTWARE on Menlo's 1998 internet and software pages was an internet resource-scheduling company Critical Path acquired in 1999. Amplitude Inc (AMPL, Nasdaq) is the product-analytics company founded in 2012. Two companies, one word.
Same distinctness as above: the 1998 Amplitude Software against the 2012 Amplitude Inc.

Menlo's Alloy is alloy.ai, the supply and demand synchronisation platform it entered at the 2021 Series A. Lightspeed's Alloy is alloy.com, the identity and fraud decisioning company. Different companies, same word.

Menlo's Axiom is the 2025-founded AI mathematician it seeded. Benchmark's Axiom is the legal-services company that was acquired — the source of the 'acquired' pre-fill this run disputed on its own row.
Menlo's Canvas is the drywall-finishing construction robotics company JLG Industries acquired in 2024. Sequoia's Canvas is a different company under the same name.
Same distinctness as above; USV's Canvas is a third company under the word.
Menlo's Check is the mobile bill-payment app (formerly Pageonce) Intuit acquired in 2014. Thrive's Check Technologies is the 2019-founded payroll API. Different companies twenty years apart.
Menlo's Clarify is the 1990s customer-service CRM company Nortel acquired in 1999. Spark's Clarify is Clarify Health Solutions, the healthcare analytics company. Different companies.
Menlo's Glide is the mobile video-messaging app that wound down. First Round's Glide is the no-code app builder. Different companies.

different companies: Menlo's Jump is JUMP Bikes (dockless e-bikes, Series A 2017, acquired by Uber in 2018); Insight's is Jump, the Salt Lake City AI assistant for financial advisors (Series B of 2026). Ruled in the TCV run's alignment pass (PRO-169), 2026-09-29.

accepted.note: Both rows are the same company (the plaintiff-side legal AI platform) and the disagreement is one of freshness: this run pinned the Sept-2025 $103M Series B at a $1B valuation, which the sibling base predates. Accepted rather than reconciled because the fix belongs on the sibling's side at wave alignment.
Same company; this run pinned the Feb-2026 $150M Series B at $1.25B, which the sibling base predates.
Same company; this run pinned the Aug-2026 $400M Series B at $5.4B, which the sibling base predates.
Same company; Databricks acquired Neon in 2025, which this run records and the sibling base predates.
Same company; Stripe agreed to acquire OpenRouter in 2026, which this run records and the sibling base predates.

Acquired against defunct for a 1990s authentication-token company that left no citable exit record on either side. The two readings differ over whether the business was bought or wound up; neither is evidenced and the row is below_1b either way, so the pair is accepted rather than forced.

Acquired against defunct for Dysan, which merged into Xidex in 1985. This run reads a merger as acquired (COLLECTION.md 6); the sibling reads the disappearance of the name as defunct. Below_1b either way.
Acquired against defunct for a 2002-era broadband gateway company; same shape as the AssureNet case and below_1b either way.

Private against acquired for LiveOps, which split into LiveOps and Serenova and passed through private-equity hands; both readings are defensible on the public record and the row is below_1b either way.
This run reads the row as private on a 2023 listing; the sibling carries unknown. Unknown is the weaker claim and the pair is accepted rather than aligned down.
Defunct against unknown for a company that wound down in 2015; unknown is the weaker claim.
Acquired against unknown; unknown is the weaker claim.
Acquired against defunct for the Fab.com European design business, which was restructured and sold on rather than wound up.
Private against unknown for a 2026 seed company Menlo led; unknown is the weaker claim.
Defunct against unknown for a campus-recruiting company that wound down around 2015; unknown is the weaker claim.
